bevel.note: chamfer size at the top edge in metres, > 0 and less than both height and half the shortest edge; switches the node to the generated-mesh lane (with UVs)

taper.note: inset of the top face in metres, > 0, along the vertex bisectors; an edge that would flip is refused with mesh_invalid; switches the node to the generated-mesh lane

axis.note: extrusion axis: "z" (default, the outline lies in XY), "x" (outline in YZ, extruded along +X) or "y" (outline in XZ, extruded along +Y); a triangle outline along x is a ramp or wedge, a pentagon a gabled block. Anything but "z" switches the node to the generated-mesh lane

metallicRoughnessMap.note: G is roughness, B is metalness; both multiply the roughness/metalness scalars on the material

uvScale.note: multiplies the UV, so smaller values repeat the texture more densely; confirm the visual direction on real hardware

normalMap.note: tangent-space normal map; the host geometry must carry tangents, which only HeightField/Lathe/Tube/Loft do - anything else is refused at compile time

emissiveMap.note: emissive map (sRGB); like baseColorMap it needs UVs but not tangents. The sampled value is multiplied by emissiveColor

emissiveColor.note: emissive multiplier [r,g,b], 0..16; 1 is the map as authored and higher values push neon past the bloom threshold. Without an emissiveMap this is a flat emissive colour

baseColor.note: the colour the surface emits directly; lighting, shadows and reflections are skipped entirely. Tone mapping and post processing still run, so this is not a pixel-exact UI colour

baseColorMap.note: sampled and multiplied by baseColor exactly as on PrincipledMaterial; needs UVs but never tangents, so any geometry can carry it

opacity.note: below 1 the surface moves to the translucent pass, which keeps the unlit path

uvScale.note: multiplies the UV, so smaller values repeat the texture more densely; confirm the visual direction on real hardware

emissiveColor.note: added on top of baseColor, 0..16. baseColor alone cannot exceed 1, so this is how an unlit sign crosses the bloom threshold

baseColor.note: the shallow-water colour, seen where the water is thin over whatever is under it. Defaults to #2f6f8f. The water lane ignores the standard material colour entirely, so this is the only colour input besides deepColor

deepColor.note: the colour the water reaches at depthFadeDistance of depth. Defaults to baseColor, which renders as a single flat water colour. The fade reads the scene depth texture, so there must be geometry UNDER the water surface for any of this to be visible - deepColor over an empty scene never appears

depthFadeDistance.note: metres of water depth over which baseColor reaches deepColor; > 0, default 150

opacity.note: 0..1, default 0.7. The water lane is always on the translucent pass and always two-sided, whatever this value is

roughness.note: 0..1, default 0; a mirror-smooth surface is what makes water look wet

specular.note: UE Specular, 0..1, default 1 (0.5 is the usual 4% dielectric F0)

waveIntensity.note: how far the scrolling normal map bends the surface normal, 0..4, default 0.103333. 0 is a perfectly flat mirror

flowDirection.note: the compass direction the normal map scrolls along, default 0, taken modulo 360

flowSpeed.note: >= 0, default 1. The surface animates with the clock, so two screenshots of the same water differ; 0 freezes it, which is what a deterministic pixel comparison needs

uvScale.note: multiplies the normal-map UV on top of the lane's built-in tiling, so larger values make finer ripples; default [1, 1] is the historical look

key.note: the KeyboardEvent.key value: "ArrowUp", "w" (letters are case-insensitive), " " (space), "Enter", "Escape". One KeyHandler claims one key.

pressed.note: true while held, false on release or when the page loses focus; readable in bindings and State.when, not writable.

autoRepeat.note: false by default: the operating system's key repeat no longer fires onPressed, so holding counts once.

button.note: which mouse button the press / drag signals follow: 0 = left (the default), 1 = middle, 2 = right. Moves and the wheel are reported whatever is held.

pressed.note: true while that button is held over the canvas; it is released again when the pointer leaves or the gesture is cancelled, so a drag cannot latch on.

hit.note: true when the cursor is over scene geometry. hitX/hitY/hitZ keep the last point that WAS hit, so guard them with this instead of looking for a sentinel value.

screenX.note: cursor position in canvas pixels, origin top-left.

screenY.note: cursor position in canvas pixels, origin top-left.

hitX.note: the picked point in the anchor's LOCAL metres, the frame every position member uses (the engine picks in earth-centred metres and the runtime converts); only meaningful while hit is true.

hitY.note: the picked point in the anchor's LOCAL metres, the frame every position member uses (the engine picks in earth-centred metres and the runtime converts); only meaningful while hit is true.

hitZ.note: the picked point in the anchor's LOCAL metres, the frame every position member uses (the engine picks in earth-centred metres and the runtime converts); only meaningful while hit is true.

wheelDelta.note: the last wheel step (the browser's deltaY: positive scrolls away from the viewer); it holds its value until the next wheel event.

dateTime.note: ISO-8601 with an explicit offset, e.g. "2026-09-12T18:30:00+08:00" (a naive instant is refused: it would mean the viewer's own timezone). This is the scene clock, and the sun, moon and stars are solved from it

timeScale.note: simulated seconds per real second; 0 stops the clock, 3600 makes one real second an hour. Negative is refused

latitude.note: site latitude for the astronomy solve; omit to follow the camera's ground point

longitude.note: site longitude for the astronomy solve; omit to follow the camera's ground point

northOffset.note: rotation of the scene's north away from true north, added to every solved azimuth

sunDiskScale.note: multiplies the sun's 0.5357 deg angular diameter

sunAzimuthOverride.note: pins the sun instead of solving it from dateTime; 0 = north, clockwise

sunElevationOverride.note: pins the sun instead of solving it from dateTime; degrees above the horizon

moonDiskScale.note: multiplies the moon's 0.52 deg angular diameter

moonPhaseOverride.note: 0..1 synodic phase (0 new, 0.5 full); omit to use the real phase for dateTime

starsIntensity.note: 0 turns the stars off; daylight fades them out on its own below 12 deg sun elevation

starsRealRotation.note: rotate the star field by the real ICRF-to-fixed matrix so constellations sit where they belong

fogGetsColorFromAtmosphere.note: true (default): the height fog takes its inscattering colour from the atmosphere, so it reddens at sunset and goes dark after it; false keeps the colour authored on ExponentialHeightFog

cloudCoverage.note: UDS CloudCoverage, 0..3 (1.14 is the Ultra Dynamic Sky factory setting). Drives the cloud layer, and with it the height fog density. Omit to leave the clouds exactly as authored on VolumetricCloud -- useful when the values came from UE

windDirection.note: direction the clouds drift toward, 0 = north, clockwise; omit to leave VolumetricCloud.noiseVelocity alone

windSpeed.note: cloud drift speed in metres per second; omit to leave VolumetricCloud.noiseVelocity alone

fogDensityClear.note: UDS HeightFog.FogDensityClear: the height fog density at cloudCoverage <= 1.1. Only applied when cloudCoverage is authored

fogDensityCloudy.note: UDS HeightFog.FogDensityCloudy: the height fog density at cloudCoverage >= 3. Only applied when cloudCoverage is authored

fogDensityDistribution.note: UDS HeightFog.FogDensityDistribution: the exponent between the clear and cloudy densities. Only applied when cloudCoverage is authored

scaleFogDensity.note: UDS HeightFog.ScaleFogDensity: multiplies the solved density. Only applied when cloudCoverage is authored

fogHeightFalloffClear.note: UDS HeightFog.ClearHeightFogFalloff. Only applied when cloudCoverage is authored

fogHeightFalloffCloudy.note: UDS HeightFog.CloudyHeightFogFalloff. Only applied when cloudCoverage is authored

detailNoiseMipDistance.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. distance in centimetres over which the detail noise drops a mip

shiftCurve.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS ShiftCurve: exponent of the cloud height gradient

zDisturbance.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS ZDisturbance: vertical disturbance of the height gradient

erosionHeightBias.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value.

erosionStrength.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value.

erosionHeightThreshold.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value.

minimumErosion.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS MinimumErosion

hightFrequencyNoiseAmount.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS HightFrequencyNoiseAmount (the UE spelling is kept on purpose)

extinctionCurve.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value.

extinctionScaleTop.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS ExtinctionScaleTop

extinctionScaleBottom.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS ExtinctionScaleBottom

nearFadeDistance.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. centimetres over which the clouds fade in near the camera

phaseG.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UE VolumetricAdvancedMaterialOutput.PhaseG

phaseG2.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UE VolumetricAdvancedMaterialOutput.PhaseG2

phaseBlend.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UE VolumetricAdvancedMaterialOutput.PhaseBlend

multiScatteringContribution.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UE VolumetricAdvancedMaterialOutput.MultiScatteringContribution

multiScatteringOcclusion.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UE VolumetricAdvancedMaterialOutput.MultiScatteringOcclusion

multiScatteringEccentricity.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UE VolumetricAdvancedMaterialOutput.MultiScatteringEccentricity

cloudSpeed.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS CloudSpeed: multiplies the clock when panning the weather map and the noise

weatherMapTileSize.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. weather map tile size in centimetres

weatherMapMipLevel.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value.

swirlScale.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS OvercastSwirl

swirlAmount.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. the swirl term of the coverage threshold; Environment.cloudCoverage writes this

swirlBias.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. the bias term of the coverage threshold; Environment.cloudCoverage writes this

emissiveColorBottom.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. cloud emissive colour at the layer bottom (linear)

emissiveColorTop.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. cloud emissive colour at the layer top (linear)

albedo.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS VolumetricCloudColor x BaseColorsScale

albedoReflection.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. albedo used while rendering reflection captures

noiseVelocity.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. cloud noise drift in centimetres per second; Environment.windDirection / windSpeed write this

noisePosition.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. UDS CloudsPosition: offset of the noise field in centimetres

noiseTiling.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. tiling of the base noise in centimetres

weatherMapVelocity.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. weather map drift in centimetres per second (z unused)

weatherMapOffset.note: Cloud material parameter, named after its UE / Ultra Dynamic Sky input so a look tuned in UE can be written here value by value. weather map offset in centimetres (z unused)

proceduralWeatherMap.note: false (default) samples the Ultra Dynamic Sky weather texture, which is what matches a look tuned in UE; true generates the weather map procedurally instead, turning weatherMapCoverage / weatherMapCloudType / weatherMapPrecipitation into real knobs at the cost of no longer matching UE

weatherMapCoverage.note: procedural weather map only: coverage on the UDS 0..3 scale. Environment.cloudCoverage writes this when proceduralWeatherMap is on

weatherMapCloudType.note: procedural weather map only: 0 stratus .. 1 cumulonimbus

weatherMapSeed.note: procedural weather map only: changes the cloud shapes

settings.autoExposureMethod.note: Histogram / Basic / Manual; Manual is fixed exposure, where the multiplier is 2^autoExposureBias

settings.autoExposureBias.note: exposure compensation; the actual multiplier is 2^bias

settings.autoExposureMinBrightness.note: lower bound of the auto-exposure white point; set it equal to MaxBrightness to lock exposure

settings.autoExposureMaxBrightness.note: upper bound of the auto-exposure white point

settings.bloomThreshold.note: bloom threshold; neon in a night scene only glows once its emission crosses it

source.note: points at a geometry node (Box/Sphere/Cylinder/Cone/Capsule/Plane/HeightField/Lathe/Tube/Loft/Sweep/Torus/Mesh/Roof/Stairs) or a fully loaded Model; the instances reuse its geometry and materials. Polygon cannot be an instance source

placement.note: explicit (give positions), grid (origin/spacing/columns/count), ring (center/radius/count, optional startAngle/faceCenter) or along_path (path plus count or step, optional alignToPath); when omitted it is inferred from whether positions was given

positions.note: per-instance positions for explicit placement, in local metres, in the same coordinate system as every other node

spacing.note: row and column spacing [dx, dy] for grid placement; both must be positive

count.note: instance count for grid placement; at most 512 per batch and 2048 per Prefab. The whole batch costs 0 additional native objects

rotations.note: per-instance rotation as [rx, ry, rz] degrees, applied roll-X then pitch-Y then yaw-Z; exactly one entry per instance, and legal under grid placement too

rotations_z.note: per-instance yaw in degrees about Z, one entry per instance; the common case for props standing on the ground

rotation_z.note: one yaw in degrees about Z for the whole batch; mutually exclusive with rotations / rotations_z

scales.note: per-instance [sx, sy, sz], one entry per instance; each component must be in (0, 10]

scales_uniform.note: per-instance uniform scale, one entry per instance, each in (0, 10]

scale.note: one [sx, sy, sz] for the whole batch; mutually exclusive with scales / scales_uniform

center.note: ring placement: circle centre in local metres

radius.note: ring placement: circle radius in metres, > 0

startAngle.note: ring placement: angle of the first instance in degrees counter-clockwise from +X (default 0)

faceCenter.note: ring placement: yaw every instance to face the centre (default false); mutually exclusive with rotations / rotations_z / rotation_z

path.note: along_path placement: polyline in local metres, 2..256 points; instances are spaced by arc length

step.note: along_path placement: arc-length spacing in metres, > 0; give either step or count

alignToPath.note: along_path placement: yaw every instance along the path tangent (default false); mutually exclusive with rotations / rotations_z / rotation_z

smooth.note: along_path placement: "none" (default) or "catmullrom" to thread the path through its points before spacing

samples.note: subdivisions per control segment under smooth: "catmullrom", integer 1..16 (default 4); refused when smooth is none or absent

heights.note: (columns+1)*(rows+1) corner heights, row-major from -depth/2; optional once noise is set, and then added on top of the noise

noise.note: "fbm": deterministic value-noise fractal (integer hash, no Math.random) sampled at every grid corner; makes heights optional

seed.note: integer 0..4294967295, required with noise; the same seed always yields the same terrain

frequency.note: noise cycles per metre, > 0 (default 0.01 = one feature per 100 m)

amplitude.note: noise peak height in metres, > 0 (default 10); the field spans about -amplitude..+amplitude

octaves.note: fbm octaves, integer 1..8 (default 4); lacunarity 2 and gain 0.5 are fixed

smooth.note: "none" (default) or "catmullrom": centripetal Catmull-Rom through the control points, end points clamped; the vertex budget and the degeneracy checks run on the resampled list

samples.note: subdivisions per control segment under smooth: "catmullrom", integer 1..16 (default 4); refused when smooth is none or absent

flat.note: hard edges along the profile (default false): every profile edge gets its own ring pair, so steps and cylinder sections meet at a crease instead of a smoothed shoulder; the circular direction stays smooth. Doubles the ring count, and a profile already rounded by smooth: "catmullrom" should not use it

smooth.note: "none" (default) or "catmullrom": centripetal Catmull-Rom through the control points, end points clamped; the vertex budget and the degeneracy checks run on the resampled list

samples.note: subdivisions per control segment under smooth: "catmullrom", integer 1..16 (default 4); refused when smooth is none or absent

smooth.note: "none" (default) or "catmullrom": the j-th point of every ring is threaded on one centripetal Catmull-Rom curve, so the surface bulges smoothly between rings; applied after resample

samples.note: subdivisions per control segment under smooth: "catmullrom", integer 1..16 (default 4); refused when smooth is none or absent

resample.note: resample every ring by arc length to the point count of the largest ring, so rings may have different point counts (each still 3..256)

closed.note: stitch the last ring back to the first (a ring-shaped loft); cap is refused when closed

profile.note: cross-section in the local XZ plane as [x, 0, z] (like Lathe), 3..256 points, counter-clockwise; local +Y is the path direction

path.note: 2..256 points; a parallel-transport frame like Tube, so a vertical first segment is fine

closedProfile.note: close the profile into a ring (default true); false sweeps an open strip such as a railing panel or a canopy

cap.note: cap both ends (default false); only with a closed profile

twist.note: total rotation of the profile about the path over its length, degrees (default 0)

scaleEnd.note: profile scale at the end of the path, (0, 10], interpolated linearly by arc length from 1 (default 1)

smooth.note: "none" (default) or "catmullrom": centripetal Catmull-Rom through the control points, end points clamped; the vertex budget and the degeneracy checks run on the resampled list

samples.note: subdivisions per control segment under smooth: "catmullrom", integer 1..16 (default 4); refused when smooth is none or absent

flat.note: hard edges across the profile (default false): every profile edge gets its own vertex band, so a square section keeps its corners instead of being smoothed into a rounded tube; the path direction stays smooth. Doubles the vertex count of a closed profile, and a profile already rounded by smooth: "catmullrom" should not use it

vertices.note: flat [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, ...] in local metres; length a multiple of 3, at most 65535 corners (the scalar_list cap of 65536 numbers allows 21845 vertices)

faces.note: flat triangle indices [a0, b0, c0, ...], integers in [0, vertexCount), counter-clockwise seen from outside

uvs.note: flat [u0, v0, ...], length 2 * vertexCount; only with it does the mesh carry UVs

shading.note: "flat" (default: every face gets its own three corners, so the vertex budget is 3 * faces) or "smooth" (corners are shared and the engine averages normals)

height.note: total height including both hemispheres; must exceed 2 * radius

segments.note: integer, at least 8 and divisible by four

radius.note: ring radius from the centre to the tube centre, > 0

tube.note: tube radius, > 0 and less than radius

footprint.note: 3..64 points forming a simple polygon (no holes, no crossings), counter-clockwise, in local metres; z of the first point is the eave height. A convex quadrilateral is planned in closed form and takes ridge; every other outline is planned from its straight skeleton and takes gables / lowEdge instead

style.note: "gable" (two slopes meeting at a ridge), "hip" (a slope per edge) or "shed" (one slope)

pitch.note: slope of the roof planes in degrees, (0, 85]

ridge.note: "auto" (default: the ridge runs parallel to the longer pair of edges), "x" or "y"; for shed it is the direction of the high edge. Convex quadrilaterals only -- a polygon derives its ridge from the skeleton and is refused if ridge is set

overhang.note: eave overhang in metres, >= 0 (default 0); refused when it turns an edge inside out

thickness.note: slab thickness in metres; 0 (default) is a single surface, > 0 builds a slab with an underside and closed edges

gables.note: polygon gable roofs only: the edge indices to finish as gable walls (edge i runs from point i to point i + 1). Omitted, every edge whose roof plane is a triangle becomes a gable (a rectangle gets the classic two, an L gets one per arm); an edge whose plane is not a triangle is refused and the message lists the ones that are

lowEdge.note: polygon shed roofs only: the index of the low eave edge the slope rises away from (default 0)

solid.note: true (default): a solid flight down to the ground; false: floating treads of thickness tread

tread.note: tread slab thickness for solid: false, > 0 (default 0.05)

landing.note: depth of a flat landing after the last step, >= 0 (default 0)

Stairs.note: starts at the origin and climbs along +X, Z up; width spans -width/2..+width/2 in Y

sprite.note: a Texture id; omit for a solid soft dot. PNG/JPEG only; alpha or greyscale decides opacity, see opacitySource

opacitySource.note: alpha (default) | luminance - greyscale smoke/glow textures without an alpha channel need luminance

emitting.note: false stops spawning and lets the live particles die; bind it to a State or Timer to switch an effect on and off

maxParticles.note: hard cap, default 500, max 20000; rate x lifetime.max must fit or the emitter clips

direction.note: local axis particles leave along, default [0,0,1] (up)

spread.note: cone half-angle around direction, 0..180; 180 is a full sphere

shapeSize.note: sphere: x is the radius; box: half extents; cone: x is the base radius

gravity.note: m/s2 pulling along -Z; 9.8 for water, ~1 for embers, negative for rising smoke

size.note: [at birth, at death] sprite edge length

sizeVariation.note: 0..1 random +/- fraction of the birth size

rotationSpeed.note: [min, max] degrees per second of sprite spin

blend.note: alpha | additive | premultiplied; additive for fire/glow, alpha for smoke/rain

softness.note: NOT AVAILABLE on this engine build: any value above 0 is refused at compile time (particle_softness_unavailable). The depth fade reaches the engine but produces no visible change on real hardware; keep it 0 and keep the effect away from surfaces it would cut into

localSpace.note: true makes live particles follow the emitter when it moves

warmup.note: pre-simulate this many seconds on creation so the effect starts full

playbackSpeed.note: 1 is real time; 0 freezes the simulation (deterministic screenshots)

seed.note: 0 is random; any other integer replays the same particles

ParticleEmitter.note: one sprite emitter; particles are unlit, do not collide and do not cast shadows
